summary: Tests-only red-phase run for issue #39. Committed: (1) the solver parity corpus fixture (byte-identical copy of viamin/color_matching priv/parity/v1/corpus.json, sha256 7b7b4d90..., algorithm_version 1) plus SolverParityCorpusTests.swift replaying all 12 scenarios — per-candidate scores/exclusions, earliest-wins selection incl. 4 tie scenarios, solver-path cross-check on a 1x1 grid; exact IEEE-754 replication of every assertion passed with 0 failures (tmp/parity-replication.py|.txt) because the container has no Swift toolchain. (2) An OpenAPI 3.0.3 snapshot fixture of the two consumed /api/v1 operations (translated 1:1 from upstream ApiSpec/ApiSchemas/ControllerSpecs, viamin/color_matching#110) plus PaletteAPIContractTests.swift pinning request/response/error wire behavior as the generated-client migration harness, and a deliberate red-phase marker testPackageShipsOpenAPIDocumentForCodegen that fails until Package.swift declares swift-openapi-generator/-runtime and a committed OpenAPI document exists. (3) docs/solver-parity-corpus.md documenting corpus + spec consumption, refresh procedures, /api/v1 shape findings (no breaking changes; spec-required name/sort_order/palette_id/printer_profile/paper_type stricter than the lenient DTO decoder; palette_name nullable; rgb optional) and parity findings (12/12 exact match at HEAD incl. ties, exclusions, unknown-weight dropping). swift test could NOT be executed — no Swift toolchain in this Linux container; the committed tests compile against the existing public API surface (verified by static review of every referenced symbol) and await execution on a macOS toolchain in the implementation run. Existing disk-cache/offline behavior evidence: 69 permanent ProfileColorCacheTests (per-server/profile namespacing, offline stale serving, removeAll/Clear Cache) remain the behavior-preservation suite for the migration.
